title: Reducedness and finite type of a Noetherian blowup
statement: Let $X$ be a reduced Noetherian scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where Noetherian means that $X$ admits a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a coherent quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent]. The ordinary blowup $b:W=\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)\to X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup] is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $W$ is reduced and Noetherian in the same convention. No integrality, nowhere-density, excellence, dimension bound or ground field is assumed. The zero ideal, unit ideal, and empty scheme are allowed.

source.place: Tags 0808, lemma-blow-up-reduced-scheme, and 02NS, lemma-blowing-up-projective; the finite-type and Noetherian consequences are included, using finite standard affine blowup charts.

proof.text: Coherence of $J$ implies that it is of finite type, by the definition of coherence. Apply the properness theorem for the blowup of a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal to $J$. It gives that $b$ is proper; since being of finite type is one of the defining conditions of properness, $b$ is of finite type. No condition on the support of $J$ occurs in that theorem.

source.place: Tag 02NS, lemma-blowing-up-projective; properness supplied by the cited blowup node

proof.text: The given finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings makes $X$ locally Noetherian. Each member is quasi-compact by the affine-scheme quasi-compactness theorem; restricting an open cover to these finitely many members and taking the union of their finite subcovers shows that $X$ is quasi-compact. Thus the Noetherian convention in the finite-type permanence theorem applies. With $f=b$, that theorem makes $W$ locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Take its affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings and use quasi-compactness to choose a finite subcover. This is precisely the Noetherian convention required in the item.

Use the given finite affine cover $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with $A_i$ Noetherian in the gluing presentation of the global blowup. The global-blowup and gluing-datum definitions specify the pieces $\mathsf B_{V_i}(J)=\operatorname{Bl}_{I_i}(\operatorname{Spec}A_i)$, where $I_i=\Gamma(V_i,J)$; the scheme-gluing theorem gives open embeddings of these pieces whose images cover the glued scheme. The cover-independence isomorphism lets us use this presentation for $W$. Each $I_i$ has finitely many generators because $A_i$ is Noetherian. Choose a list $(a_{ij})_j$, using the one-element list $(0)$ when $I_i=0$. The finite affine chart-cover theorem gives charts $\operatorname{Spec}C_{ij}$ with $C_{ij}=A_i[I_i/a_{ij}]$ covering each piece, hence covering $W$.

Every $A_i=\mathcal O_X(V_i)$ is reduced by the sectionwise characterization of reduced schemes. Here is the fraction calculation for a chart, including zero divisors. Write $A=A_i$, $a=a_{ij}$ and $C=A[I_i/a]\subseteq A_a$. If $c=x/a^n\in C$ and $c^m=0$ with $m\geq1$, the definition of localization gives $a^N x^m=0$ for some $N\geq0$. Choose $e$ with $em\geq N$. Then $(a^e x)^m=a^{em-N}a^Nx^m=0$, so $a^e x=0$ because $A$ is reduced. The same localization equality criterion now gives $c=0$. Thus $C$ is reduced; this uses neither injectivity of $A\to A_a$ nor cancellation of $a$.

The affine reducedness criterion makes each $\operatorname{Spec}C_{ij}$ reduced. For every $w\in W$, choose one of the open charts containing $w$. Its local ring at $w$ is the local ring $\mathcal O_{W,w}$, because the chart is an open subscheme. That local ring is reduced. The stalkwise definition of a reduced scheme therefore says that $W$ is reduced.

For $J=0$, the chart list $(0)$ has coordinate ring $A[0/0]\subseteq A_0=0$, so all its spectra are empty and $W$ is empty. For $J=\mathcal O_X$, take the chart list $(1)$: its ring is $A[A/1]=A$, and the structure maps are identities. If $X$ is empty the gluing has no nonempty pieces, so again $W$ is empty. The same arguments apply to the zero ring and to reduced rings with several components. Thus no edge case requires integrality or a nonempty complement to the center.
